merger_name: Australian Venue Co – Assets of Riverland Bar, The Boatbuilders Yard and General Assembly

targets.name: DOG AT THE BRIDGE PTY LTD

party_page.name: Dog At The Bridge Pty Ltd

merger_description:
AVC Operations Pty Ltd (**AVC**) proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets (including the exclusive right to carry on the businesses in succession of the vendors and the benefit of the leases) of three licensed hospitality businesses in Victoria pursuant to one sale agreement (**Sale Agreement**) of the three businesses trading as “The Boatbuilders Yard” (**Boatbuilders Yard**), “General Assembly” (**General Assembly**) and “Riverland Bar” (**Riverland**), with certain assets excluded from the sale (the **Acquisition**).

AVC is a subsidiary of Australian Venue Co. Holdings Limited which operates over 200 licensed venues throughout Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars, clubs and licensed restaurants. AVC's venues are individually branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metropolitan areas, offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and gaming facilities.

The three abovementioned businesses (the **Businesses**) are standalone sites and provide different offerings, including:

* Boatbuilders Yard is a pub located at 23 South Wharf Promenade, South Wharf, VIC 3006
* General Assembly is a pub located at 29 South Wharf Promenade, South Wharf VIC 3006
* Riverland is a pub located at Federation Wharf Vaults 1-9, Melbourne VIC 3000.

The Businesses are currently owned and operated by entities associated with the Riverland Group, a retail hospitality group.

determination_table_content.details:
AVC Operations Pty Limited (AVC) applied for a notification waiver in
respect of its proposed acquisition of substantially all of the assets
of three licensed hospitality businesses in Victoria, being: i) the
business trading as Riverland Bar (Riverland Bar), ii) the business
trading as The Boatbuilders Yard (The Boatbuilders Yard), and iii) the
business trading as the General Assembly (General Assembly)
(together, the Targets), as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, AVC, operates over 200 licensed venues throughout
Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars,
clubs and licensed restaurants. AVC's venues are individually
branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metropolitan areas,
offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic
and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and
gaming facilities.
The targets, Riverland Bar, The Boatbuilders Yard and General
Assembly, are associated with the Riverland Group, a retail
hospitality group that operates licensed venues across Victoria
(primarily in Melbourne) as well as one business in South Australia,
comprising primarily pubs, bars and licensed restaurants.
The parties both supply retail hospitality services in metropolitan
Melbourne.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition:
a. the parties combined share in the supply of dining and on-
premises liquor services in the local areas surrounding the
Targets is low
b. there are alternative venues that supply dining and liquor for
on-site consumption in the local areas surrounding the
Targets and the in the broader metropolitan Melbourne area.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
